title: Clinical Decision Support and Health Data Platform Landscape
summary: Assessment of clinical decision support platforms and claims data analytics capabilities serving life sciences, covering evidence-based medicine databases, claims datasets, and their integration with commercial CRM workflows.

findings.cds_platform_components: Clinical decision support platforms combine drug reference databases, evidence-based clinical content, and diagnostic decision support tools. Key databases: drug interaction databases (covering 2M+ drug-drug interaction pairs), evidence summaries, and condition-specific treatment protocols.
findings.claims_data_assets: Healthcare claims datasets covering 200M+ lives provide longitudinal patient journeys across pharmacy, medical, and hospital claims. These datasets are essential for: treatment pattern analysis, physician prescribing behavior, patient switching studies, and market sizing.
findings.commercial_integration_gap: CRM platforms and claims data platforms operate in separate ecosystems. Field teams need claims-derived insights (prescribing trends, patient volumes, treatment patterns) embedded in their CRM workflows rather than requiring separate analytics logins.
findings.competitive_landscape: Multiple vendors compete across clinical content (evidence databases), claims analytics (prescribing patterns), and real-world evidence (outcomes analysis). Consolidation is creating larger platforms that span content, data, and analytics.
findings.strategic_implications: For CRM platforms serving life sciences, the opportunity is integrating third-party clinical and claims data into field workflows — providing medical affairs teams with evidence context and commercial teams with prescribing intelligence without requiring separate platform licenses.

source: Assessment of clinical decision support platforms and health data capabilities for life sciences commercial operations
